findings.title: Customers keep queueing at a till the player picked up in build mode, and follow it around the store
findings.detail: `BuildMode.pick()` has no customer check. `sell_refusal` refuses with "Someone is at this till" (build_mode.gd:241-244), but nothing stops you moving a checkout while people are queued or being served. Build mode can also be opened while the store is OPEN (`enter()` only checks your hands and tool). Once the till is carried, `_checkout_ok()` only checks that it is valid, in the tree and not queued for deletion. It never calls `world.in_use(checkout)`, unlike `_slot_has` at :232. So `_queue_tick` keeps running and `_queue_walk` calls `queue_spot_for()` every tick from the ghost's live `global_transform`. Queued customers walk after the floating till. `Checkout._physics_process` can also `begin()` the front customer and unload items onto the moving counter. Fix: in `pick()`, refuse a `Checkout` with `customer`, a non-empty `queue` or a cashier, the same way `sell_refusal` does. Also add `and shopper.world.in_use(checkout)` to `_checkout_ok()`, so a carried till sends its queue to `_join_queue()`.
findings.note: customer_test regression (till with queue can't be picked up; carried till's queue moves)

findings.title: The front customer at an unstaffed till never moves to a till that is being served
findings.detail: `Checkout._physics_process` calls `begin(queue[0])` as soon as the front customer is `ready_at_till()`, whether or not anyone is serving; it only rings the bell. `begin()` sets them to AT_TILL. The AT_TILL branch of `_queue_tick` never calls `_maybe_switch_queue()`, which only runs in QUEUE. A common case: you serve at till 1, a cashier works till 2, and you leave to restock. The C5 fix moves everyone behind the front customer to till 2. The front customer stands at till 1 with their basket on the counter for the full 90 s of `patience_s`, then drops the basket and leaves. That is lost sales, a mess and about −15 satisfaction, while the cashier at till 2 has nobody to serve. Fix: in the IDLE branch, only `begin()` when `is_attended()` or no attended till with room exists. Otherwise leave them in QUEUE so the 2.5 s switch check can move them.
findings.note: checkout_test regression fails before, passes after

findings.title: Each list entry buys one unit, and repeated entries for the same product stack penalties and contradict each other
findings.detail: This confirms the lead. `pick_list` draws with replacement, so the same product can appear on a list several times. Each entry is a separate trip, price roll and `remove_one`. An unstocked product listed twice costs −12 twice (−24) and two lost sales; the second bark is dropped because they are still talking. At +40% the customer can say "I'm not paying $X for that" and grab the same item 0.3 s later (refuse chance 16% per roll). Nobody buys a six-pack's worth, as Supermarket Simulator customers do. Fix: turn the list into `{id: qty}` and merge duplicates. Draw the quantity from a new `customers.json` `quantity` table, optionally per product. Make one price decision and one OOS or refuse penalty per product. Take `min(qty, stock)` units across slots and show all of them in the basket.

findings.title: Customers buy items they physically cannot reach
findings.detail: `_stand_point` snaps the spot 0.6 m in front of the slot to `nav.closest()`, which can be metres away when that spot is blocked. `BuildRules.refusal` has no rule keeping slot fronts clear, so two shelves can be placed face to face with a gap under 0.6 m, or a shelf front against another fixture's back. TO_SLOT then calls `_reach_in()` whenever `follow()` returns true or they stop walking, with no distance check. The customer takes stock from the end of the aisle, through a shelf. `_nearest_slot` also ranks slots by straight-line distance through fixtures, so it prefers such a blocked slot. Fix: in `_stand_point`, if the snapped point is more than about 0.3 m from the intended one, treat the slot as unreachable and try the next nearest. Check that the customer is within 0.5 m of the stand point before `_reach_in`. Add a front-clearance rule (about 0.7 m) to `BuildRules.refusal`.
findings.note: Build-rule half of N4 (front clearance) also landed

findings.title: No crowd avoidance: customers pass through each other and walk through the player, who cannot get past them
findings.detail: This confirms the lead. `collision_mask = Mk.LAYER_WORLD` for shoppers, and staff and Dale do the same. The ARCHITECTURE doc says this is deliberate ("people pass through each other"). Everyone walks to the exact same `DOOR_IN` point, the exact same stand point for a slot, and one of two spawn points. The spawner's `while pending` loop (customer_spawner.gd:41-43) can spawn several customers in one frame at the same `EXITS` point, so they walk the same path inside each other. The player's mask includes `LAYER_NPCS`, so it is one-sided. Customers walk into your capsule, and the physics probably pushes you out when you next move [INFERENCE: Jolt depenetration]. Meanwhile someone picking an item, or an overflow queuer told to "wait where they are" for up to 90 s, blocks your way down a 1 m aisle completely. Fix: add `LAYER_NPCS | LAYER_PLAYER` to the walker mask. Use navmesh avoidance (`NavigationServer3D` agents with `velocity_computed`) or a cheap separation steer. Spread out stand points and `DOOR_IN` per customer, and space out spawns.
findings.note: nav_test: head-on walkers keep >0.35 m and still arrive; windowed tour ran clean

findings.title: Trolleys go through shelves at every pick and every corner
findings.detail: The trolley sits at `TROLLEY_OFFSET` (0, 0, −0.78), in front of the body. The checkout code says it sticks out about 0.9 m. The stand point is only `REACH_STAND` = 0.6 m from the slot front, and `_reach_in` turns the body to face the shelf. The trolley's origin ends up about 0.18 m inside the fixture, with most of its length inside. Paths are planned for a 0.3 m agent radius, so the trolley also cuts through shelf ends at every turn. R2's C8 fixed this only at the till. Fix: trolley users stop beside the shelf. Leave the trolley at the stand point lined up with the aisle (`top_level`), and face the shelf from beside it. Or add the trolley length to the stand distance and to a larger nav radius for trolley customers.

findings.title: Customers know an item is out of stock without looking, and complain wherever they happen to be
findings.detail: `_find_slot_or_lose` checks every slot in the store instantly. With none in stock, the "No {product}? Seriously?" bark and the −12 happen where the customer is standing, often by the door or at the previous shelf. findings.title: Customers keep staring back at the shelf for 2.5 s after a bark at the shelf
findings.detail: `tick` only resets `look_weight` while `not bark.is_talking()`. At the shelf the weight is 1 with `look_target` on the slot front. A forced refusal bark or a `great_prices` bark then moves the state to BROWSE. The weight stays at 1 for the 2.5 s bark, and the target is not updated unless you are within 4 m. The customer walks to the next item with their head turned up to 70° back at the old shelf. When you are nearby, they stare at where you stood when they started talking. Fix: drop `look_weight` to 0 when leaving PICK unless they are talking to you. While talking within 4 m, update `look_target` to the player camera every tick.

findings.title: The arrival cap counts customers walking along the footpath and through the car park
findings.detail: `live_count()` counts everyone in the `shoppers` group. Customers start and end at `EXITS` (−22.5, 29.5) and (16.5, 29.5), about 38 m and 35 m in a straight line from `DOOR_IN`. At 1.2–1.6 m/s that is roughly 22–32 s each way, about 45–60 s of every visit spent outside, all counted against `2 + 4·tills + level/2`. With 6 slots on day 1, a large share are on the pavement while the store sits empty. The spawner, `Game` CLOSING and the open sign also wait for that walk. Fix: leave customers in LEAVE who are past the door out of the cap, keeping the hard 20 for performance. Or start and end them at the parked-car bays (`ParkedCars`), much closer to the door.

findings.title: Fair, well-run service cannot earn more than about 3.85 stars
findings.detail: Satisfaction starts at 70, which is already 3.5 stars, and the only positive events are bargain (+3, only at ≤85% of market), promo (+2 once) and fast service (+5). A fully stocked, fairly priced visit with quick service ends at 70 + 5 + 2 = 77, or 3.85 stars. Any single out-of-stock (−12) drops it below 3.5. `fast_service_s` = 20 s counts from joining the queue, including the walk to the lane and 0.35 s per item to unload (`UNLOAD_STEP`), so trolley customers rarely get it. The M9 soak sits at 3.04 stars on day 30. Good play is not rewarded unless you sell below market. Fix: add positive events in `customers.json`, such as found every item (+8), a fair price at or under market (+1 per item), and a clean store (+3). Or lower `start` and rebalance.

findings.title: Basket and bag follow the hands one frame late from physics

findings.title: Paying bills with negative cash makes every bill bigger
findings.detail: `complete_sale` adds `sale.net()` to `money` without a floor. `net()` is `charged - over_changed`, and the change tray has no limit (`checkout.gd:681-684` appends any note). So handing over a $100 note by mistake when cash is low, which is common on day 1 after spending the $600 on stock, leaves `money` below zero. In `pay_bills`, `part := mini(money, cents)` is then negative. `b["paid"] = part` stores that negative number, and `unpaid = cents - part` becomes `cents + |money|`. Each of tonight's bills goes overdue at its full amount plus the whole cash deficit, plus 10% on top. With four bills, the deficit is counted four times. The receipt sees `paid < 0`, so it shows no PAID or UNPAID tag. Fix: `var part := clampi(money, 0, int(b["cents"]))` in both loops, and the same in `pay_overdue`.

findings.title: The third short night ends the game with no warning, no way out, and wrong advice on screen
findings.detail: Only a night that ends with nothing overdue resets `overdue_streak`; paying the debt off at the Bank in the morning does not. The receipt tells the player "Pay them at the Bank on the PC", so they clear everything. The Bank then hides the streak, because `_fill_overdue` returns "Nothing overdue." before it draws the warning. If they end that night even 1¢ short, repossession is certain. Holding E on the sign gives no warning. On the receipt the only button is "Pay all", and `loan_refusal` returns "The bank is closed" in SUMMARY, so they can't borrow to cover it. The run is lost with no chance to react; only the clipboard's red total hints at it. Fix: show the streak in the Bank and the HUD whenever it is above 0. When streak + 1 would reach `repossession_days` and cash is below `bills_due()`, block or confirm End day at the sign. Allow loans in SUMMARY before Pay all. Change the receipt text to "Clear them and cover tonight's bills, or the bank takes the store on night N".

findings.title: Customer numbers don't grow with store size, so expansions E4–E8 and tills 5–6 only add cost
findings.detail: The in-store cap is `min(20, 2 + 4·tills + L/2)`. Floor area plays no part, and the cap is already 20 with 4 tills from L4, or 3 tills from L12. Arrivals above the cap wait in `pending` and are thrown away at 22:00 (`customer_spawner.gd:28-31`). Buying E4–E8 adds $25–40 a day in rent plus $1.50 a cell in electricity for no extra customers; E8 alone is $7,500. Tills 5–6, sold up to `max: 6`, can't raise the cap. The M9 soak in PROGRESS.md shows customers flat at about 101–117 a day from day 14 to day 30. The AI held $3k–6k cash on days 21–24 and still didn't expand, and it never bought E6–E8. The end of the build-out is a trap. Fix: make the cap depend on unlocked floor area or cells, e.g. `base + per_till·tills + per_cell·cells`, with a higher hard cap. Also correct the stale comment and defaults at customer_rules.gd:34-37, which still say `4 + 2·tills`.

findings.title: The pacing table is not met, but M9 was recorded as passed
findings.detail: The table promises: day 7 "E3, dairy + frozen"; day 15 "E5–E6, 2–3 tills, staff", $900–1,600; day 30 "E8 full store", $2,500+. Across the three soak runs, day 7 is still the start store, day 15 has only E1 and E3 with $837–895, and day 30 has E5 with $1,977–2,194. Every day-15 and day-30 money figure is below its band and only passes with the ±25% tolerance. Not one Store-column row is met. The data file also stores day 1 as level 1 and day 30 as level 15 with profit `[250000, 250000]`, while the doc says 1–2, 15–16 and "+". Fix: retune (E3 fixes the store column), or rewrite the table to what the game actually does and stop calling M9 met.

findings.title: The soak AI prices at +10%, so money pacing was never checked for real players
findings.detail: ECONOMY.md says profit per shopper is best at +25–55%, but the bot always sells at market +10%. A rough estimate from soak run 1, day 15 [INFERENCE]: $1,976 revenue, about $410 of bills, cost of goods about $718. At +40% with about 10% more refusals, profit comes to roughly $1.2k instead of $848, about 40% more. Real players will build up cash much faster than the tuning assumed. Levels then become the only real gate, and licence and expansion purchases stop being money decisions. Fix: run the soak with a 35–40% markup, or one per elasticity band, and retune costs and prices against that.

findings.title: Every loan's daily instalment is at least the whole day's profit when it unlocks
findings.detail: Small loan at L1: $108 a day against a day-1 profit of $40–120. Business loan at L5 (about day 7): $560 a day against $250–450. Expansion loan at L10 (about day 15): $1,643 a day against $848–895 in the soak. Terms are 10–14 days, and the first instalment is charged the same night. Taking any of them leads straight to overdue bills and, under E2, repossession, unless what you buy pays back the full instalment from the first day. PROGRESS M9 confirms the soak AI had to be stopped from borrowing except for tills and licences. In practice the choice is "never borrow". Fix: longer terms, e.g. 30/40/60 days with the same interest, or instalments set to about 40% of the expected daily profit at the unlock level.

findings.title: Fair prices top out around 3.85 stars, and stars fall as you level up
findings.detail: Satisfaction starts at 70 (3.5★). The only gains are +3 per item sold at ≤0.85× market (a loss-leader), +2 once near a promo stand, and +5 for fast service. A perfect visit at market price or above therefore peaks at 77, about 3.85★. 4.5★ needs about five loss-leader items per customer, so the newspaper's "worth crossing town" headline can't be reached without selling below market. Lists grow with level (`1 + randi()%(2+L)`), and each item adds another −12 out-of-stock chance, so stars sink as you progress: the soak shows 3.6 at L5 against 2.2–3.0 at L8–16. Stars only scale arrivals by `0.4 + 0.12·stars`, and once E3's cap binds they don't matter at all. Fix: add positive events (item found, clean store, short queue, a well-stocked basket), or score satisfaction relative to the list size.

findings.title: Progression runs out around day 27, and two of the 16 levels unlock only a colour
findings.detail: Max level is 16, which the soak reaches on day 27. Nothing exists after it: no prestige, no new licences, no reason to keep earning, and E3 makes the late expansions worthless anyway. L13 unlocks only a sky blue uniform and L16, the final level, only a hot pink trim. L7 is just S2 and L11 just S3. Fix: move a real unlock to L13 and L16 (a till tier, staff tier 3, an extra loan, a product line), and add post-cap goals such as weekly targets or a second store.

findings.title: The day-length option changes income while bills stay the same
findings.detail: Arrivals are counted per in-game hour (`delta * clock.rate()`), but walking, shopping and checkout take real seconds, and the cap counts shoppers alive in real time. Once the cap binds, customers per day are roughly cap × real day length ÷ visit time. An 8-minute day serves about a third fewer customers than a 12-minute one [INFERENCE: 20 × 480 s / ~150 s ≈ 64 against ≈ 96]. A 20-minute day serves more, yet rent, wages and loans are charged per day. Picking "short days" in Options quietly cuts income and pushes the player toward overdue bills. Fix: scale the cap or arrival rate by `12 / day_length_min`, or tune and soak at each option.

findings.title: Shoppers turned away by the cap are never shown
findings.detail: `pending` arrivals that never got in are silently zeroed at 22:00. They are not recorded as lost sales, not on the receipt, and not in Stats or the newspaper. The player has no way to see that a second till or a bigger cap is what's holding income back. Supermarket Simulator's feedback is about what customers do; here the biggest income limit can't be seen at all. Fix: count `turned_away` in DayReport, show it on the receipt and in Stats ("23 shoppers gave up at the door, add a till"), and add a "left without entering" bucket to the weekly review.

findings.title: The receipt leaves out most of the day's spending, so its net doesn't match the change in cash
findings.detail: "Net after bills" is sales minus cost of goods minus bills. Stock orders, the $5 delivery fees, furniture, licences, expansions, hire fees, staff upgrades, loan payouts and repayments, and fixture refunds don't appear anywhere. A typical day-2 receipt shows "+$150" while cash fell $400 after a restock and a licence, and there is no opening-cash line to reconcile against. Supermarket Simulator's end-of-day report itemises expenses [UNVERIFIED]. Fix: total `money_changed` deltas by reason in `today` (`spent[reason]`, `opening_cash`), and print "Spent today" lines plus "Cash at open → Cash now".
findings.note: day_test: open + sales + other = cash now

findings.title: The store can't close early or skip time during OPEN
findings.detail: Once the sign is OPEN it only says "OPEN until 22:00", and the clock has no fast-forward. On days 1–3 the four starter kinds sell out by mid-afternoon. The player then waits about 6 real minutes for 1–2 shoppers, which is dead time. Supermarket Simulator lets you flip the sign closed early [UNVERIFIED]. Fix: allow E on the sign during OPEN to go to CLOSING, with a confirm. Optionally allow a hold-to-fast-forward while nobody is in the store.

findings.title: The newspaper says a product "kept running out" when it may have been refused for price
findings.detail: `missed` comes from `lost_products`. `_count_lost_sale` adds to that for every reason: out of stock, too expensive and left the queue. `body()` then prints "%s kept running out" using the top of that mixed count. A product that was overpriced and never ran out gets named as the stock problem, which is the wrong advice. Fix: keep `lost_products` per reason, or a separate `oos_products`, and name the out-of-stock leader there.

findings.title: Early payoff of the Expansion loan on its last day costs more than letting it run
findings.detail: The daily instalment is $1,643 against an exact $1,642.857, so at k=13 `remaining` is 164,100. `payoff` after hours is `2,000,000·1/14 + roundi(21,428.6)` = 164,286. "Repay now" charges $1.86 more than the final instalment it replaces. Fix: `return mini(principal_left(loan) + roundi(...), int(loan["remaining"]))`.

findings.title: Receipt profit uses today's cost, not what was paid for the stock

Costs drift up to ±15%, so stock bought cheap and sold on an expensive day shows less profit than was really made, and the reverse. A player who times orders for cheap days never sees the gain on the receipt or in Stats. Fix: carry the purchase cost per box or slot (average cost) and book that on sale.

commits.subject: Make not carrying a product a milder letdown than an empty shelf
commits.body:
Customers took the full -12 out-of-stock hit for products the store never sold, so a new store
was punished for its range rather than its stocking. An empty labelled slot is still -12; a
product with no slot at all is -4 with its own lines. Still a lost sale (the demand signal).
Review round 2, cycle 2.

commits.body:

the rest. Loading now puts the excess in an open box in front of the fixture. Also keeps test
and tour cash out of the receipt's other-money lines. Review round 2, R10.

commits.subject: Draw cans at real size, one layer deep: 30 to a cooler shelf instead of 6
commits.body:
The can models were built twice real size, so a 24-can box needed four cooler shelves and
cans emptied in minutes. products.json model_scale scales them wherever they are drawn (keeping
the import LODs); COLA, FIZZ, BEER and SOUP sizes now match real cans. Checked in the screenshot
tour. Review round 2, S3.

commits.subject: Say why Order is greyed out, and let Shift add or remove five boxes in the Market
Say why a restocker stands idle: no boxes on the stockroom racks
Make walkers keep personal space and pass head-on to the right
commits.body:
Customers and staff walked straight through each other and through the player. A light
separation steer (0.7 m, plus keep-right for anyone just ahead) keeps them apart without
changing their paths. Review round 2, N5.

commits.subject: Make customers shop like people: walking order, complaints at the empty shelf, shared doors
commits.body:
- They walk to an empty labelled slot before complaining, so you can see which shelf is bare (N7).
- A long list is shopped nearest-first instead of zig-zagging the store (N13).
- A customer leaving a cooler doesn't shut it on another still reaching in; the job passes on (N16).
- The walk animation follows the actual movement (no striding on the spot against a wall) (N17).
- Idle loops start at each person's own phase, so queues don't breathe in step (N19).
- Customers go home the way they came instead of nearly all leaving east (N20).
- GDD list length and picking rules brought up to date (N22).
Review round 2.

commits.subject: Read the start state and level cap from data, show an expansion's full running cost, and warn about short days
commits.body:
- new_game reads start level, XP and cleanliness from settings.json; the sandbox picker, dev
  flag and main menu read the level cap from levels.json and the money range from one place;
  unused customers.json keys removed (E19, N23).
- The Expansions card shows rent plus lights before and after, not rent alone (E18).
- Options says shorter days fit fewer customers while bills stay the same (E9).
Review round 2.

commits.subject: Give levels 13 and 16 real unlocks: loyalty cards and a head office franchise
commits.body:
Both only unlocked a colour, and nothing paid off after the level cap. Loyalty cards (L13,
$3,000) add 3 satisfaction per paying customer; the franchise (L16, $10,000) pays $100 a star
every Sunday night, shown on the receipt and in the paper. Upgrade effects live in
upgrades.json. Review round 2, E8.

commits.subject: Stretch loan terms to 20/30/40 days so borrowing is a real choice
commits.body:
At 10-14 days every instalment was at least the day's whole profit when the loan unlocked, so a
loan led straight to overdue bills and repossession. Same interest, smaller instalments. Loan
and bills tests now read the numbers from loans.json. Review round 2, E6.

commits.subject: Itemise the day's other money on the receipt so it adds up to the cash
commits.body:
Orders, furniture, licences, expansions, staff, upgrades and loans never showed, so a '+$150'
night could end with less cash than the morning. The receipt now lists them and the cash at
open (saved with the day). Review round 2, E11.

commits.subject: Show on the receipt how many customers a full store turned away
commits.body:
Arrivals held back by the in-store cap were dropped silently at closing, so the player never
learned that another till or cashier would have earned more. Review round 2, E10.

commits.subject: Name the product that actually ran out in the Sunday review
commits.body:
'Kept running out' used the top of all lost sales, so an overpriced product that never ran out
was blamed. Out-of-stock misses are now counted (and saved) on their own. Review round 2, E13.

commits.subject: Reward visits that go right, free the cap from people walking home, and fix four customer slips
commits.body:
- +8 when everything on the list was found at a fair price, +4 in a 90%-clean store: good play
  now ends visits around 4.35 stars instead of topping out near 3.85 (N10, E7).
- Customers already out of the door on the way home no longer hold places under the in-store
